## Buying office furniture in Newcastle starts with a usable brief

For a growing Newcastle, Lake Macquarie or Hunter business, furniture decisions connect people, the floor plan, the budget and the move-in plan. Start those conversations together rather than choosing products first and checking the building later.

This guide is a practical purchasing framework. Product prices, availability, installation scope and professional advice need to be confirmed for your particular workplace; they are not established by a general local price range or headcount rule.

## Record how the workplace will actually be used

Ask the people using the office about busy-day attendance, concentrated work, video calls, meetings, storage and visitors. Separate workstations needed at the same time from the total number of people on the payroll. Record any individual adjustment or accessibility needs that should inform the brief.

Build a simple schedule before approaching suppliers:

| Part of the brief | What to record | Question to resolve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workstations | Peak simultaneous users, equipment and tasks | Which settings are assigned or shared? |
| Meeting spaces | Meeting types, group sizes and technology | What needs an enclosed room? |
| Seating | Users, adjustments, daily use and floor surface | Can suitable options be assessed or trialled? |
| Storage | Items to store, access and security needs | What existing storage can be retained? |
| Growth | Confirmed changes and possible later additions | What should be ordered now versus kept as an option? |

Helpful tip: mark uncertain quantities clearly. A possible future hire is different from an approved workstation required on opening day.

## Use a measured plan, not a universal area allowance

Check actual room dimensions, columns, door swings, services and the size of furniture in use, including chair movement and open drawers. Test the layout with your designer or relevant adviser before relying on a catalogue image or a square-metres-per-person shortcut.

SafeWork NSW's [Managing the work environment and facilities code](https://www.safework.nsw.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0016/50074/Managing-the-work-environment-and-facilities.pdf) discusses clear space for movement, access and evacuation, alongside workstations suited to people and tasks. A furniture sketch alone does not confirm building, access or workplace compliance.

Helpful tip: measure the delivery route as well as the room. A product can fit its final position while still being difficult to bring through a doorway or lift.

## Build a budget from specifications and installed quotes

A useful furniture budget identifies what is being bought, what can be reused and what services are included. Compare the same quantities, sizes, finishes and performance requirements before comparing totals. Ask whether GST is included and keep product costs separate from freight, assembly, placement, packaging removal and any other agreed services.

Do not assume a per-person figure includes reception, meeting rooms, breakout seating, storage or technology accessories. Record those items separately. Use current written quotes for decisions, with a clear expiry date and a note of assumptions that still need checking.

[Plan your furniture budget](/blog/office-furniture-budget-newcastle) and [compare installed furniture quotes](/blog/compare-office-furniture-quotes-installed-cost).

Helpful tip: show an alternative product or quantity as a separate option. That makes a lower headline price easier to assess without losing the original specification.

## Confirm availability for the actual product and finish

Ask the supplier to distinguish stock available for allocation from goods that must be manufactured or ordered. Confirm the product code, quantity, finish, delivery destination and any dependencies before relying on an estimated arrival date.

A product's manufacturing origin does not, by itself, establish the delivery date, warranty service or future matching availability. Ask how a delay, substitution, damaged item or incomplete order would be handled. Record who can approve changes and how they affect the programme and price.

[Compare standard, modified and custom furniture](/blog/standard-modified-custom-office-furniture-newcastle).

Helpful tip: separate an estimated dispatch date from delivery and installation readiness. Confirm each milestone and leave unconfirmed dates labelled as estimates.

## Assess the workstation as a whole

Compare the chair, desk, screens and input devices together, with the people who will use them. Adjustment options are useful only if they suit the task and users know how to use them. Request the relevant product specifications and discuss assessment or trial options where available.

[Comcare's computers and workstations guidance](https://www.comcare.gov.au/office-safety-tool/spaces/work-areas/computers-workstations) covers equipment adjustment, tasks, different users and setup instruction. It is practical ergonomic guidance, not a product endorsement or a substitute for a workplace-specific assessment. Ask a suitable WHS or ergonomic adviser about individual needs or concerns rather than treating a desk type or the word “ergonomic” as proof of suitability.

Helpful tip: record the required adjustments and equipment compatibility in the quote brief, so seating or desk alternatives can be compared against the same needs.

## Check Newcastle delivery and installation arrangements early

Confirm the requirements for the particular building with its manager. Avoid assuming every Newcastle CBD, Honeysuckle or suburban property has the same access rules.

- Record loading access, parking or booking arrangements and the contact for arrival.
- Check lift capacity and dimensions, stairs, doorways and the route to the final position.
- Agree any induction, insurance evidence, work-hour restrictions or protection requirements for the site.
- Confirm whether assembly, positioning, adjustments and packaging removal are included.
- List furniture being retained, relocated or removed, and confirm who handles each part.
- Record how completion, damage and outstanding items will be checked and followed up.

[Prepare the furniture installation checklist](/blog/office-furniture-installation-checklist-newcastle).

Helpful tip: give the supplier an annotated plan with product labels that match the order schedule. Identify one person who can resolve placement questions on delivery day.

## Check reuse, warranty and future additions separately

Inspect existing furniture before assuming everything needs replacing. Record condition, dimensions, adjustment functions and compatibility with the proposed layout. Confirm any relocation or repair work needed to make reuse practical.

For new products, read the written warranty terms: intended use, exclusions, claim process and any associated service or transport arrangements. Ask about replacement parts and finishes, but treat future supply as uncertain unless the supplier gives a specific commitment.

[Audit furniture for reuse](/blog/office-furniture-reuse-audit-newcastle).

## Frequently asked questions

### How much should a Newcastle business budget for office furniture?

Build a schedule covering products, quantities, specifications, reuse and delivery services, then obtain current comparable quotes. A general per-person allowance does not establish the cost of your workplace. Keep unquoted items and assumptions visible until they are confirmed.

### How long does office furniture take to arrive?

Ask for written availability and delivery estimates for the exact products, quantities and finishes. Distinguish allocation, manufacturing or ordering, dispatch, site delivery and installation. Reconfirm dependencies before tying a move-in decision to an estimate.

### Can a small business plan furniture without a designer?

The support needed depends on the layout, building, users and project scope, not a universal team-size threshold. A supplier can help clarify product specifications; involve the relevant designer, building adviser or other professional where the brief requires their expertise.

### Should we choose height-adjustable desks?

Assess the tasks, users, existing equipment and adjustment needs as part of the workstation brief. Ask for relevant product information and suitable ergonomic advice where needed. A product choice alone does not establish that the whole workstation or workplace is suitable.
